system_description.narrative_title: Diplomatic push to stabilize the Strait of Hormuz amid US–Iran hostilities
system_description.narrative_summary: Regional diplomacy — led by Oman and picked up by Saudi, Iran and the US — is driving a focused effort to create management mechanisms for the Strait of Hormuz as periodic US–Iran strikes pause. Treated as an open system, the story links cross-border flows (tankers, oil, weapons), state and non-state actors (Iran, US, Oman, Saudi, Houthis), and market signals (oil prices, insurance, inventories) with fast feedback loops: attacks spike prices and insurance; pauses lower them and create space for negotiations and commercial normalization. Immediate catalysts (missile strikes, talks, Omani proposals) repeatedly shift incentives across military, diplomatic and commercial actors, producing volatile but interdependent outcomes for global energy security.
system_description.scope: Inside the boundary: the Strait of Hormuz transit system and adjacent shipping lanes (including Bab el-Mandeb/Red Sea), regional states (Iran, Oman, Saudi Arabia, UAE), the US military and diplomatic posture, Iran-backed militias (Houthis, Iraqi militias), oil markets (Brent/WTI, futures, inventories, SPR), shipping/insurance markets, energy firms and trade flows, and near-term events (missile strikes, US strikes, Omani proposals, talks).
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitics-energy-financial system (global energy security and international security architecture)
adjacent_subsystems: Global crude and refined products markets & trading
Regional maritime security (Red Sea, Bab el-Mandeb) and shipping logistics
Military operations, deterrence postures and escalation dynamics
Energy supply chain resilience (refining, SPRs, LNG) and insurance markets

variables.name: Global oil price level
variables.description: The prevailing market price level for crude oil measured as a representative global benchmark index.

variables.name: Maritime transit rate through chokepoints
variables.description: The volume or count of commercial vessel transits through key regional sea lanes per unit time.

variables.name: War-risk insurance premium level
variables.description: The average premium level charged for war-risk and political-risk insurance on regional maritime shipments.

variables.name: Rate of military strikes and kinetic incidents
variables.description: The frequency of kinetic attacks, strikes or intercepts in the maritime and adjacent operational area per unit time.

variables.name: Maritime security commitment intensity
variables.description: The aggregate level of security operations, patrols and defensive deployments dedicated to protecting regional shipping routes.

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement intensity
variables.description: The volume and intensity of sustained diplomatic interactions and negotiations aimed at managing regional tensions.

variables.name: Concentration of control over transit corridors
variables.description: The degree to which authority and effective control of key maritime transit corridors are centralized or monopolized.

variables.name: Oil export flow volume through the region
variables.description: The rate of crude oil and petroleum product exports transiting the regional sea lanes measured in barrels per day.

variables.name: Spare oil production capacity
variables.description: The available unused upstream oil production capability that can be brought online within a short to medium timeframe.

variables.name: Strategic petroleum reserve level
variables.description: The quantity of government-held emergency petroleum stocks available for release to stabilize supply.

variables.name: Market volatility expectation
variables.description: The market-implied expectation of near-term price volatility for oil and energy markets.

variables.name: Degree of commercial normalization
variables.description: The extent to which commercial actors (shippers, insurers, traders) resume pre-crisis operational patterns and risk tolerances.

variables.name: Non-state maritime militia activity
variables.description: The intensity and operational tempo of non-state armed groups conducting attacks or interdictions affecting maritime traffic.

variables.name: Alternative route and transit capacity
variables.description: The available throughput capacity of alternate shipping routes, pipelines, and terminals to absorb rerouted flows.

variables.name: Energy supply disruption risk
variables.description: The aggregated probability and expected severity of disruptions to energy supply reaching global markets via the region.

catalysts.title: Oman-led Hormuz negotiation push
catalysts.description: Oman and Gulf states press a regional management proposal for the Strait of Hormuz, with meetings between Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia continuing.

catalysts.title: Near-term U.S. strikes escalation cycle
catalysts.description: U.S. commanders and leadership signal a planned two-week escalation of strikes and reprisals against Iran-linked targets, raising kinetic activity risk.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "The U.S. Commander With a Two-Week Plan to Escalate Strikes"; "Trump Pledges Retaliatory Strikes"; recent U.S. strikes.

catalysts.title: Saudi-led multinational maritime coalition buildout
catalysts.description: Saudi Arabia's announced plan to form a multinational maritime defence coalition progresses toward formal commitments and deployments to protect shipping.

catalysts.title: Houthi Red Sea activity and fee proposals
catalysts.description: Houthis continue attacks and explore charging transit fees in the Red Sea, potentially expanding interdictions and commercial friction along alternate routes.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Houthis say they targeted Saudi east-west oil transport"; "Houthis considering fees..."; Red Sea attacks slowing shipping.

catalysts.title: OPEC+ likely pause on output hikes after September
